title: A Current for the Compass
premise: Oscar Lockridge, who learned to read soil better than their father ever taught them to read people, is working a salvage crew on a windswept coast when an unprecedented low tide exposes the mouth of the Hollow of Saint Verren — a cave that local legend says grants truth and takes payment in memory. Inside, Oscar finds their estranged father's expedition team trapped by a collapsing tide gate, along with evidence that he faked his greatest discovery. To bring everyone home alive, Oscar must navigate the cave's disorienting passages, broker peace between rival crew members, and decide whether loyalty means protecting their father's lie or telling the truth that will destroy him. In the end, Oscar leads the survivors out, lets the sea reclaim the cave, and publicly reports the fraud — losing their father but gaining, at last, a family that chose them back.
about_author: P. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent a decade charting coastlines before turning to fiction full-time. They write adventure novels from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage, where the tide still dictates the writing schedule.

chapters.title: The Long Way Around Stopping
chapters.summary: Oscar Lockridge's POV. Oscar arrives in the fishing town of Greyharbour with a salvage crew, already planning their exit before unpacking. Flashbacks reveal why they never stay anywhere: every place they stopped became a place they lost someone. Emotional beat: restless self-protection masking loneliness.

chapters.title: What the Tide Owes
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A once-in-a-century low tide strips the bay bare, revealing a stone archway locals refuse to name. Old fisherman Bram Corrigan tells the legend of the Hollow: it shows you what you most need to see and keeps what you can't bear to lose. Oscar, skeptical, photographs the entrance anyway. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding caution.

chapters.title: Lockridge, Senior
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The famous archaeologist Edmund Lockridge arrives in Greyharbour leading a funded expedition — and his first act is hiring his estranged child, publicly, as a digger. Their brittle reunion crackles with old wounds. Oscar accepts for reasons they won't admit. Emotional beat: pride and hunger tangled together.

chapters.title: Into the Hollow
chapters.summary: POV alternates between Oscar and expedition photographer June Okafor. The team enters the cave at slack tide; phosphorescent mineral veins light passages that seem to rearrange. June sees her late brother; Oscar hears their mother's voice. When the tide turns early, the exit floods shut. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into entrapment.

chapters.title: The Room of Small Truths
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Trapped deeper in, the team finds Edmund's secret camp: he'd been here months ago, and the 'discovery' funding this expedition is fabricated — plaster casts and planted artifacts. Edmund begs Oscar to help conceal it until they're out. Crew member Devan overhears. Emotional beat: betrayal reopening every old scar.

chapters.title: Water Finds Its Level
chapters.summary: June's POV. Rising water splits the group. Oscar takes charge of the stranded half while Edmund leads the others toward a secondary passage that may not exist. June watches Oscar become, under pressure, everything their father never was. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing in crisis.

chapters.title: Payment in Memory
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Alone in a flooded gallery, Oscar confronts the cave's heart — a chamber where their own memories play out, including the night their mother left and the lie Edmund told about it. They understand the legend now: the cave doesn't take memory, it returns it. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into clarity.

chapters.title: The Second Passage
chapters.summary: Devan's POV. Devan, furious about the fraud, threatens to leave Edmund behind. Oscar reaches the group in time to force a reckoning: Edmund confesses to the whole team, and Devan, shaken, agrees to move together. The secondary passage opens onto a rising shaft. Emotional beat: truth as survival, not punishment.

chapters.title: Against the Turning
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Climax. With the tide at its peak, Oscar maps an escape through submerged siphons using techniques their father taught them — the one inheritance worth keeping. Edmund nearly drowns saving June; Oscar pulls them both through the final gap as the cave seals. Emotional beat: courage earned, not inherited.

chapters.title: A Current for the Compass
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Weeks later, Oscar files the report that ends Edmund's career, then stays in Greyharbour — the first place they've chosen to remain. Bram teaches them the tides; June and Devan become family. Edmund writes one letter; Oscar reads it, keeps it, and doesn't answer yet. Emotional beat: stillness chosen, not imposed.
